sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami Pg.196).

paras: Hadhrat Ummu Hakeem (RA) says, "I was still a little girl when Hadhrat Husayn was martyred. For a few days afterwards, the sky remained the colour of a blood clot."
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.196).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Qubayl says, "When Hadhrat Husayn (RA) was martyred, the sun eclipsed so extraordinarily that stars were visible at noon and we really thought that Qiyaamah had arrived." ''* In his Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah (Vol.8 Pg.201), Allaama Ibn Katheer has cited all the above narrations apart from the first as weak, categorising them as fabrications of the Shias. Allaah knows best.

Hadhrat Maalik bin Dinaar reports that when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was martyred, a voice (of a Jinn) was heard coming from the Tabaalah mountains (in Yemen). It recited the following couplets (which mean): "1 stand at the service of whoever wished to weep over (the adherents to) Islaam because their destruction is imminent even though much time has not yet elapsed This world is leaving with all its good And those people have lost interest in this world who aspire for the Aakhirah "
When the people looked to see where the voice came from, they could see no one.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.197).

paras: Hadhrat Ma'roof Mowsili narrates that he heard a voice reciting some couplets when Hadhrat Umar (RA) was martyred. The narration then proceeds to quote the above two couplets.
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.94).

paras: Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) says, "Although I could see no one, I heard someone lamenting the death of Hadhrat Umar (RA) one night as he recited the following couplets (which mean): "May Allaah reward the Ameerul Mu'mineen with the best rewards and may Allaah 's hand bless the skin that has been ripped apart (O Ameerul Mu'mineen) Whoever walks or rides to achieve the accomplishments you have attained to catch up with what you have accomplished in the past, he will surely be beaten You have accomplished tremendous feats but then left behind such tragedies, the buds of which have still to bloom"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il (Pg.210). Tabraani has reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id ' (Vol.9 Pg.79).

paras: Hadhrat Sulaymaan bin Yasaar reports that the Jinn mourned the death of Hadhrat Umar' by reciting the following couplets (which mean): "Peace be on the Ameerul Mu'mineen and may Allaah 's hand bless the skin that has been ripped apart (O Ameerul Mu'mineen) You have accomplished tremendous feats but then left behind such tragedies, the buds of which have still to bloom Whoever walks or rides to achieve the accomplishments you have attained to catch up with what you have accomplished in the past, he will surely be beaten The martyrdom of such a personality in Madinah has caused darkness to loom over the earth After this, can the acacia tree ever allow its branches to sway in the breeze?"
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Dalaa'il (Pg.210).

paras: In another narration, Hadhrat Aa'isha (RA) quotes the above four couplets in a different sequence, but then adds another couplet (which means) : "(O Ameerul Mu'mineen) May my Rabb meet you with salutations in Jannah and with the garments of Firdous that never tear"
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 9 Pg.199).

paras: (Ummul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) says, "The Jinn were heard bewailing the death of Husayn bin Ali.
sources: Tabraani. Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.199) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Another narration states that Hadhrat Ummu Salamah (RA) once said, "Since the demise of Rasulullaah ﷺ, I have never heard the Jinn lament the death of anyone as I hear them do tonight. I think that my son (Hadhrat Husayn (RA)) is now deceased." She then instructed her maid servant to make enquiries, after which she learnt that Hadhrat Husayn (RA) had been martyred. She further reports that a lady from the Jinn was then heard reciting the following couplets (which mean): "O my eye! Take careful note of my exertion because (if I do not) who will weep after me over that group of people whose deaths lead them to tyrants in the service of mere slaves"
(Ummul Mu'mineen) Hadhrat Maymoona (RA) says, "The Jinn were heard lamenting the death of Husayn bin Ali.
sources: Tabraani, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.199).

paras: Hadhrat Abu Moosa Ash'ari (RA) says, "1 saw myself at place where there were many roads. All the roads started to vanish until there was only one left. I then took the road, which led me to a mountain. On top of the mountain stood Rasulullaah ﷺ, with Abu Bakr beside him. Rasulullaah ﷺ was gesturing to Hadhrat Umar (RA) to come there. 1 then said to myself, 'Innaa Lillaahi wa Innaa Ilayhi Raaji'oon! I swear by Allaah that Ameerul Mu'mineen will be leaving this world.'"
To this, Hadhrat Anas (RA) said, "Why do you not write to Ameerul Mu'mineen about this." Hadhrat Abu Moosa (RA) replied, "I cannot inform him of his own death."
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.99), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi. (3) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.75). Abu Ya'la has reported a similar narration, but Haythami (Vol. 7 Pg.232) has commented on the chain of narrators.

paras: Hadhrat Katheer bin Silt narrates, "On the day Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) was martyred, he happened to fall asleep (during the day). He then woke up an said, 'I would inform you of something had it not been for people saying that Uthmaan wishes to stir trouble.' 'May Allaah mend your affairs,' we said, 'Please do inform us because we will not say what other people say.' He then related, 'I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ in the sleep I just had and he said to me, "You will be with us this Friday.
sources: Haakim (Vol.3 Pg.103), reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Dhahabi. Abu Ya'la and Bazzaar have reported a similar narration, as quoted in Majma'uz Zawaa'id (Vol.7 Pg.232), lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.74) has also reported a similar narration.

paras: Another narration adds that that very day was Friday.
sources: Abdullaah and Abu Ya'la, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol. 7 Pg.232). Majma'uz Zawaa'id 'and Al Bidaayah wan Nihaayah state several other narrations of the same.

paras: Hadhrat (RA) reports that Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) related to them one morning that he saw Nabi ﷺ telling him in a dream, "O Uthmaan! Terminate your fast with us." Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) therefore fasted that day and it was on that very day that he was martyred.
sources: Adani.

paras: Hadhrat Muslim Abu Sa'eed who was a freed slave of Hadhrat Uthmaan bin Affaan says, "Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) set twenty slaves free and then asked for a pair of trousers, which he wore, even though he never wore trousers at any time before Islaam or after becoming a Muslim. He then said, 'Last night I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ, Abu Bakr and Umar. They said to me, 'Be patient because you will terminate your fast with us tomorrow evening.' He then asked for his Qur'aan and opened it before him (to recite). He was later martyred with the Qur'aan still in front of him."

Hadhrat Hasan (RA) or Hadhrat Husayn (RA), reports that (their father) Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, "I met my beloved friend (Nabi ﷺ) in a dream and when I complained of the problems I am having with the people of Iraq after he had left this world, he promised me deliverance from them in the near future." It was barely three days later that he passed away.

Hadhrat Abu Saalih says, "Hadhrat Ali (RA) once said, '1 saw Nabi ﷺ in a dream and complained to him about the way in which his Ummah are falsifying me and harming me. When I started to cry, Rasulullaah ﷺ said, 'Do not cry, O Ali. Turn around.1 When I turned around, I saw two men bound in fetters, whose heads were being crushed by boulders. Each time, their heads were crushed, they were then restored, after which the process continued.' The following day, I was proceeding on my way to meet Hadhrat Ali (RA) as 1 did every day, but as 1 was passing by the place where butchers gathered, I met some people who informed me that the Ameerul Mu'mineen had been assassinated."
sources: These two were probably Hadhrat Ali (RA)'s assassin Ibn Muljim and his accomplice.

paras: Hadhrat Filfila Ju'fi reports that he heard Hadhrat Hasan bin Ali (RA) say, "1 saw in a dream that Nabi ﷺ was holding on to the Arsh. I then saw that Abu Bakr was holding on to Nabi ﷺ's waist, that Umar was holding on to Abu Bakr's waist and that Uthmaan was holding on to Umar waist. Then I saw blood extending from the sky to the earth." When Hadhrat Hasan (RA) was relating this dream, there happened to be some members of the Shia sect with him, who then asked, "Did you not see Ali Hadhrat Hasan (RA) replied, "There is none I would not have loved to see holding Nabi ﷺ's waist more than Ali. Nevertheless, that was the dream that I saw..." The narration continued further.
sources: Abu Ya'la, as quoted in Muntakhab Kanzul Ummaal '(Vol. 5 Pg.61).

paras: Hadhrat Hasan (RA) once said, "O people! I saw a most remarkable thing in my dream last night. I saw the Rabb the Most High upon the Arsh. Rasulullaah ﷺ then arrived and stood by one of the feet of the Arsh. Thereafter, Abu Bakr arrived and placed his hand upon Rasulullaah ﷺ's shoulder. He was followed by Umar, who placed his hand upon Abu Bakr's shoulder, after which Uthmaan arrived and placed his hand upon Hadhrat Umar (RA)'s shoulder. Uthmaan then gestured with his hand and said, 'O my Rabb! Ask Your servants why they killed me.1 Two downpipes of blood then started to flow from the sky to the earth."
Someone reported this to Hadhrat Ali (RA), saying, "Do you not see what (your son) Hasan is saying?" Hadhrat Ali Slav's reply was, "He is only relating what he saw."

Another narration states that Hadhrat Hasan (RA) added, "1 shall not fight again after the dream that I saw..." The narration then proceeds like the one above, but with the difference that he said, "I then saw Uthmaan with his hand upon Umar's shoulder. Thereafter, I saw a lot of blood behind them. 'What is this?' 1 enquired. I was then informed that this was the blood of Uthmaan for which he was asking redress from Allaah."
sources: Tabraani in his Awsat and Kabeer, reporting from reliable sources as confirmed by Haythami (Vol.9 Pg.96).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) reports, "In my afternoon sleep, I saw Rasulullaah ﷺ with dishevelled hair and with a glass in his hand. 'What is this glass for?' I asked. 'The blood of Husayn and his companions. I have been picking it up all day.' When we then saw the date, we found it to be the same day in which Husayn was martyred."
sources: Khateeb in his Taareekh (Vol.1 Pg.142). Ibn Abdul Birr has reported a similar narration in his Isti'aab (Vol.1 Pg.381).

paras: Hadhrat Abbaas bin Abdul Muttalib (RA) says, "I was the neighbour of Umar bin Khattaab and have never seen anyone better than him. His nights were spent in salaah and his days were spent fasting and tending to the needs of people. When he passed away, 1 asked Allaah to show him to me in a dream. In a dream one night I saw him coming form the marketplace of Madinah with his shawl draped over his neck. After exchanging greetings, I asked, 'How are you?' '1 am well,' he replied. 'What did you find?' I asked further. He replied, 'My reckoning is now over. Had I not found a Merciful Rabb, my honour would have fallen."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol. 1 Pg.54). (3) lbn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.375).

paras: Hadhrat Abbaas (RA) relates, "Umar bin Khattaab was my very good friend. After he passed away, I made du'aa to Allaah for a complete year to show me Umar in a dream. The year had just come to an end when I saw him wiping perspiration from his forehead. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen!' I said, 'How did your Rabb treat you?' 'My reckoning is now over,' he replied, 'Had I not found a Forgiving and Merciful Rabb, 1 would have fallen in honour.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.375).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) says, "I made du'aa to Allaah for a year to show me Umar bin Khattaab in a dream. When I saw him in a dream, I asked, 'How was your experience?' He replied, 'I found a Most Forgiving and Merciful Rabb. Had it not been for His mercy, I would have fallen in honour.

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Umar (RA) says, "There was nothing I wanted more than to know what had happened to Umar (in the next life). I then saw a palace in a dream and when I asked whom it belonged to, I was informed that it belonged to Umar bin Khattaab. He then came out of the palace wearing a shawl, appearing as if he had just taken a bath. 'What has happened to you?' I asked. 'I have been well,' he replied, 'but had I not found a Forgiving Rabb, I would have fallen in honour.' He then asked, 'How long ago did I separate from you?' 'It is twelve years now,' I replied. He then said, 'I have just now returned from my reckoning.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.54).

paras: Hadhrat saalim bin Abdullaah reports that he once heard an Ansaari say, "I had always prayed to Allaah to show me Umar bin Khattaab in a dream. It was after ten years that I did see him wiping perspiration from his brow. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen!' I said, 'What has happened to you?' He replied by saying, 'I have just completed my reckoning and had it not been for the mercy of my Rabb, I would surely have been destroyed.
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.376).

paras: Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) was returning from Hajj when he (set up camp and) fell asleep at a place called Suqya. When he woke up, he said, "I just saw Umar (in a dream). He walked up to me and used his foot to nudge (my wife) Ummu Kulthoom bint Uqba who was asleep beside me. This woke her up and he then went away. As the others went out in search of him, I also got my clothing, dressed and went out to search with them. Although I was the first to catch up with him, I swear by Allaah that I found him only after I had thoroughly exhausted myself. 'O Ameerul Mu'mineen!' I said, 'You have really made it difficult for the people (to keep up with you). By Allaah! One can only catch up with you after thoroughly exhausting themselves. In fact, it was only after I had thoroughly exhausted myself that I managed to catch up with you.' To this, he said, 'But I do not think that I had been going fast at all.'
I swear by the Being Who controls the life of Abdur Rahmaan that this (lead over the rest of us) was because of his deeds."
sources: Ibn Sa'd (Vol.3 Pg.376).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam Si reports that Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once said to him, "Dear brother! Whichever of us dies first should make an attempt to see his brother." "Is such a thing possible?" Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) asked. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, "Certainly. (After death) The soul of a Mu'min is free to roam wherever it wills on earth, whereas the soul of a Kaafir is locked in captivity."

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Salaam (RA) says, "Salmaan passed away and I was lying on my bed one afternoon when I happened to fall asleep. Salmaan then appeared in my dream and greeted me saying, 'As Salaamu Alayka wa Rahmatullaah.' I responded by saying, 'As Salaamu Alayka wa Rahmatullaah, 0 Abu Abdullaah. How have you found your destination?1 He replied, 'It is excellent. Hold fast to Tawakkul because Tawakkul is a most excellent virtue! Hold fast to Tawakkul because Tawakkul is a most excellent virtue! Hold fast to Tawakkul because Tawakkul is a most excellent virtue!.
sources: Ibnsa'd (Vol.3 Pg.4).

paras: Another narration states that when Hadhrat Abdullaah (RA) saw Hadhrat Salmaan in a dream, he asked, "How are you faring, O Abu Abdullaah?" "I am well," came the reply. "Which deed did you find to be most virtuous?" Hadhrat Abdullaah asked. Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) replied, "I have found Tawakkul to be most remarkable."

Hadhrat Auf bin Maalik (RA) relates, "I saw a leather tent and a green pasture in a dream. Around the tent there sat goats that ruminated and excreted Ajwa dates. When I asked whom the tent belonged to, 1 was informed that it belonged to Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf. We then waited for him to emerge and when he did, he said, 'O Auf! This is what Allaah has given me because of the Qur'aan. If you look yonder over that valley, you will see things that your eyes have never seen before, that your ears have never heard of and the thought of which has never crossed your heart. Allaah has prepared it for Abu Dardaa because he used to shove the world away with both his hands and chest.
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Hilya (Vol.1 Pg.205).

paras: Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Amr bin Haraam (RA) says, "Before the Battle of Uhud I saw Mubashir bin Abdul Mundhir in a dream. He said to me, 'You will be coming to us in a few days.' 'Where are you?' I enquired. He replied, 'In Jannah where we are able to roam wherever we please.' I then asked him, 'Were you not killed in the Battle of Badr?' 'Yes,' he replied, 'but we were then brought back to life...'" When this was reported to Rasulullaah ﷺ, he remarked, 'Such is martyrdom, O Abu Jaabir."
sources: Abu Nu'aym in his Pg.210).
